subject.title: fix(cli): abort reaps autonomous executor process trees

question: Should ACPX startup and abort fail closed whenever OpenClaw cannot verify and fully drain the turn-owned runtime lease?
rationale: Best-effort cleanup preserves availability but can leave a credentialed autonomous executor acting after abort; fail-closed cleanup enforces the user’s stop boundary but changes compatibility and failure behavior for existing ACPX workflows.

options.title: Guarantee verified drain
options.body: Require a verifiable per-turn ACPX lease and fail startup or cancellation unless all verified owned descendants are drained.

options.title: Allow best effort
options.body: Close the runtime handle and attempt cleanup, but allow startup or abort completion when complete survivor ownership cannot be verified.

recommendation.title: Guarantee verified drain
recommendation.body: Require a verifiable per-turn ACPX lease and fail startup or cancellation unless all verified owned descendants are drained.

likelyOwner.reason: The current process-supervisor ownership architecture originated in this contributor’s merged work, making them the strongest history-based routing candidate for this boundary decision.
